dedupe_keys.name: feedus netlogo agent based model of global food trade and food and nutrition security

description: FeedUS is a global food trade model written in NetLogo by Jiaqi Ge and published in the CoMSES library in 2021 (version 1.2.0). Its purpose is to study how global food trade affects food and nutrition security in countries around the world. Trade between countries depends on three aspects: each country's wealth, its geographic location and its past and ongoing trade relationships with others. The model is meant for scenarios such as climate change, sustainable intensification, waste reduction and dietary change. The code is available as a free download from CoMSES under the MPL-2.0 licence. Caveats: the library page describes the design, partly in the future tense, but gives no calibration data or validation, so it is best treated as a research prototype. Coverage is global, at country level. Simulation uses: exploring how trade networks spread supply shocks between countries and which countries' food security depends on them. Related records: DARTS (model-darts-food-system) is a related agent-based model of food system shocks, and USDA PSD Online (data-usda-psd-online) supplies commodity balances by country.
inputs: Country wealth, geographic location and past and ongoing trade relationships
name: FeedUS: NetLogo agent-based model of global food trade and food and nutrition security
outputs: Food trade flows and food and nutrition security by country under scenarios
